lines.text: What if every animal on Earth vanished, except us?
No birdsong at dawn. The barn is empty, and the fields are perfectly still.
On day one, breakfast changes. No eggs, no milk, no meat.
Every cow, chicken and pig on the planet is simply gone.

segments.caption: The empty lake
segments.fact: FISH GIVE THEM 20% OF ANIMAL PROTEIN

lines.text: Fishing boats come back with empty nets.
More than three billion people get a fifth of their animal protein from fish. Now there's none.
Then spring comes, and the flowers wait for bees that never arrive.
Most of our leading crops rely on animals to carry their pollen.
The orchards bloom, but no fruit forms. Apples, almonds, coffee and cocoa start to disappear.
Prices soar, and diets shrink to bread and rice.
But we won't starve completely. Wheat, rice and corn are pollinated by the wind.
And fungi and bacteria aren't animals, so dead leaves still rot back into soil.

segments.caption: Humans become bees
segments.fact: DONE IN SOME ORCHARDS IN CHINA

lines.text: So people climb ladders with brushes, pollinating flowers by hand, as some farmers in China already do.
It's slow, expensive work, on billions of trees.
We'd survive, hungrier and poorer, on a far quieter planet.
But would it still feel like home? Which animal would you miss the most?
